data.standardized_narrative: Syndicate 1200 opened 2017 with gross claims outstanding of GBP 586.6m (2016 comparative). During 2017 the syndicate recorded an overall adverse prior-year development of GBP 53.7m driven principally by the exceptionally severe catastrophe activity in 2017 (Hurricanes Harvey, Irma and Maria, California wildfires and Mexico earthquakes) and adverse development in short-tail classes (notably US Direct & Facultative, Cargo, Yachts & Hull) where rate pressure and unsustainable loss emergence required strengthening of reserves.
raw_causal_phrases: the worst year for catastrophes in the US for over a decade with Hurricanes Harvey, Irma and Maria, the wildfires in California and earthquakes in Mexico causing insured market losses of $135 billion, the costliest year on record (source: Munich Re).

Syndicate 1200 has also had to strengthen loss reserves predominantly in short tail lines of business that have seen the most rate pressure in the market over the last four years, namely US Direct & Facultative, Cargo, Yachts & Hull.
These lines have seen rate reductions of up to 50% in the last 4 years as well as unsustainable losses developing well in excess of the expected level.
In 2017, there has been an overall deterioration of GBP 53.7m (2016: improvement of GBP 1.6m).

The deterioration in these classes of business during 2017 (and to some extent 2016) led us to make certain underwriting decisions during 2017 (to reduce aggregate US property exposures, harden our stance on rate adequacy, and exit certain sub sectors of the individual classes e.g. garden style habitational property).

data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development figure used is the report narrative statement ('overall deterioration of GBP 53.7m') because no explicit separate 'movement in prior year's provision' gross reconciliation was provided. A gross claims development triangle is present and a triangle-based subtotal for 2012-2015 gives +GBP 40.5m (gross) - the narrative GBP 53.7m includes older aggregate years (2011 & prior) which the triangle aggregates and cannot be disaggregated. The triangle contains an aggregate '2011 and prior' column which cannot be used to compute a per-year diagonal; therefore narrative gross figure was preferred. Movements by LOB are computed from the gross outstanding claim balances (2017 vs 2016) and therefore include current year influences and foreign exchange; they are provided for directional insight but are not the same as the 'prior year development' number.
